To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) there was a significant difference between the system designs produced when the data-centered methodology was used and when the process-centered methodology was used, (b) there was a statistically significant difference in the quality of the system design produced when the data- and process-centered methodologies were used and when no methodology was used, and (c) the data-centered methodology did not produce a significantly better system design than the process-centered methodology.
“The data-centered system development method did not produce system designs that were superior to those produced by a process-centered methodology.”
1. The data-centered methodology was not significantly better than the process-centered methodology for producing system designs of high quality for a data-intensive application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficacy of matching the application characteristics with the system development methodology.

the question of whether the application of a system development methodology to an application problem is more likely to produce better results than the application of no system development methodology at all.

determining the impact of system development methodologies on the quality of system designs and the impact of application characteristics (such as data-intensiveness) on the quality of the resulting designs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study indicate that the use of a data-centered methodology did not produce system designs that were significantly better than those produced by a process-centered methodology for a system problem that was intentionally constructed to be data-intensive in nature.
the data-centered and process-centered methodologies are equally effective when applied to a system design problem.
the use of a data-centered system design methodology does not produce significantly better system designs than a process-centered methodology for data-intensive systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
system development methodologies are not as important as system development skills.
the development of “strongly typed methodologies” for information system development may not be a worthwhile endeavor.
there is no evidence that the application of a specific system development methodology is more effective than the application of a more generic system development methodology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
system development methodologies may not need to be tailored to specific application development technologies.
the quality of the resulting system design was not dependent on the methodology used, but rather on the quality of the analysis and design performed.
a good methodology is one that is taught well.
